This mask ensures that only occlusion from the upper hemisphere defined by $n$ contributes to the ambient occlusion integral [S1].

The claim states that the mask ensures only occlusion from the upper hemisphere defined by normal $n$ contributes to the integral. The evidence in Source [S1] explicitly states: 'Considering that AO of the point x only calculates the occlusion integral of the upper hemisphere Ω of the normal n, we thus conduct masked-trilinear interpolation...'. It further defines the masked weight $w̃_k$ as 0 if $(p_k - x) · n ≤ 0$ (i.e., the direction is not in the upper hemisphere) and $w_k$ otherwise. This confirms that the masking mechanism restricts the contribution to the upper hemisphere.

Every Frame enables continuous capture for dynamic occluders [S2, unofficial].

This confirms that 'Every Frame' enables continuous capture for dynamic occluders.

Standard trilinear interpolation weights $\{w_k\}$ are modified to $\{\tilde{w}_k\}$ by zeroing out contributions from volumes where the vector from the sample point to the volume center has a non-positive dot product with the surface normal ($ (p_k - x) \cdot n \le 0 $) [S1].

The claim states that standard trilinear interpolation weights are modified by zeroing out contributions where the dot product of the vector from the sample point to the volume center and the surface normal is non-positive. Source [S1] explicitly defines the masked trilinear interpolation weights $ ar{w}_k$ in Equation (20) as: $ ar{w}_k = 0$ if $(p_k - x)  ullet n  lacksq 0$, and $ ar{w}_k = w_k$ otherwise. This ensures that ambient occlusion is only calculated from the upper hemisphere relative to the surface normal, preventing incorrect shadowing from below [S1].

The claim states that ambient occlusion is calculated only from the upper hemisphere relative to the surface normal to prevent incorrect shadowing. The evidence in Source [S1] explicitly states: 'Considering that AO of the point x only calculates the occlusion integral of the upper hemisphere Ω of the normal n, we thus conduct masked-trilinear interpolation to get the correct coefficients.' It further details the mechanism where weights are zeroed out if the vector from the point to the volume is not in the direction of the normal (i.e., (pk - x) · n ≤ 0), which effectively restricts the calculation to the upper hemisphere.
